title: Hook Type Modernization
brief: Add prompt, agent, and HTTP hook types alongside existing command hooks. Currently all hooks are command (shell script) type. Prompt hooks use lightweight LLM evaluation, agent hooks spawn verification subagents, HTTP hooks POST to endpoints.

phases.title: New Hook Types + Migration
phases.description: Implement prompt, agent, and HTTP hook types. Migrate top bash checks to prompt hooks. Document hook type selection.

units.title: Prompt hook — code quality check
units.rationale: Bash-based code quality checks are brittle and miss semantic issues. LLM prompt hooks can evaluate edit quality holistically — checking naming, patterns, consistency, and intent alignment.
entry_conditions: Claude Code supports prompt hook type in settings.json
exit_conditions: Prompt hook evaluates Edit/Write tool outputs for quality
Catches naming violations, anti-patterns, missing JSDoc
Response includes specific improvement suggestions
units.rollback: Remove prompt hook entry from settings.json

steps.instruction: Define prompt hook schema in settings.json: type='prompt', event='PostToolUse', prompt template with {{tool_output}} placeholder
Write prompt template that evaluates: naming conventions, JSDoc presence, error handling, TypeScript strictness
Configure filter: only trigger for Edit and Write tool calls on .ts files
Set response action: warn (not block) for quality issues
Test with sample edits: good code passes, bad code triggers warnings

deliverables.description: Prompt template for LLM-based code quality evaluation on Edit/Write outputs

units.description: Prompt hook — code quality check — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Prompt hook — commit message quality
units.rationale: Commit messages should follow consistent conventions. LLM evaluation catches vague messages, missing context, and style violations better than regex.
entry_conditions: Prompt hook type working from P0-U01

Evaluates: length, specificity, verb tense, scope
Good messages pass through without delay

Write prompt template evaluating: imperative mood, <72 char subject, body explains why not what, references issue/milestone
Set response action: block with suggested rewrite for failing messages
Test with good and bad commit messages

units.title: Prompt hook — safety gate
units.rationale: Destructive operations (force-push, delete, reset) need semantic validation beyond pattern matching. LLM can understand context and intent to make better safety decisions.
entry_conditions: Prompt hook type working from P0-U01
exit_conditions: Destructive operations require LLM approval
Context-aware: allows 'rm temp.txt' but blocks 'rm -rf src/'
Approval/denial includes reasoning
units.rollback: Remove prompt hook entry from settings.json

steps.instruction: Define prompt hook for PreToolUse on Bash tool calls
Write prompt template: classify command as safe/caution/dangerous, evaluate blast radius, check for data loss potential
Set response action: block for dangerous, warn for caution, pass for safe
Include context: current branch, recent changes, working directory
Test with spectrum: safe commands, ambiguous commands, clearly dangerous commands

deliverables.description: Prompt template for LLM-based destructive operation safety evaluation

units.title: Agent hook — physics verification
units.rationale: Physics engine edits risk introducing formula regressions. An agent hook spawns a verification subagent that cross-checks formulas against known-good references.
entry_conditions: Claude Code supports agent hook type
exit_conditions: Formula regressions caught on engine file edits
Agent verifies dimensional consistency, constant values, model names
Verification runs in <30s
units.rollback: Remove agent hook entry from settings.json

steps.instruction: Define agent hook in settings.json: type='agent', event='PostToolUse', filter on *Engine*.ts files
Configure agent: model=haiku, maxTurns=5, tools=[Read,Grep], prompt='Verify physics formulas in edited file'
Agent checks: Kienzle kc formula structure, Taylor tool life exponents, dimensional consistency (force=N, speed=m/min)
Agent outputs: pass/fail with specific formula locations
Test with deliberate formula corruption and verify detection

deliverables.description: Agent hook definition for physics formula verification on engine file edits

units.title: Agent hook — test impact analysis
units.rationale: Running all 17K+ tests after every change is wasteful. An agent hook analyzes which tests are impacted by code changes and suggests targeted test runs.
entry_conditions: Claude Code supports agent hook type
exit_conditions: Targeted test subset identified after code changes
Agent traces imports to find affected test files
Suggested test command output with specific files
units.rollback: Remove agent hook entry from settings.json

steps.instruction: Define agent hook: type='agent', event='PostToolUse', filter on Edit/Write of .ts files
Configure agent: model=haiku, maxTurns=10, tools=[Read,Grep,Glob]
Agent traces: edited file → imports → test files that import edited file
Agent outputs: list of affected test files + suggested vitest command
Test with edits to engines, dispatchers, and shared utilities

units.title: Agent hook — schema validation
units.rationale: Dispatcher schemas must match engine signatures. Schema drift causes runtime errors. An agent hook verifies schema-engine alignment after dispatcher edits.
entry_conditions: Claude Code supports agent hook type
exit_conditions: Schema mismatches caught on dispatcher/schema edits
Agent verifies z.enum entries match engine exports
Agent checks action handler signatures match schema fields
units.rollback: Remove agent hook entry from settings.json

steps.instruction: Define agent hook: type='agent', event='PostToolUse', filter on *Dispatcher*.ts and *Schema*.ts files
Configure agent: model=haiku, maxTurns=10, tools=[Read,Grep,Glob]
Agent checks: z.enum entries exist as exports, handler signatures match schema fields, action names consistent
Agent outputs: pass/fail with specific mismatches listed
Test with deliberate schema-engine misalignment

units.title: HTTP hook — telemetry endpoint
units.rationale: Session metrics, tool usage patterns, and error rates need real-time visibility. HTTP hook POSTs metrics to a local dashboard endpoint for live monitoring.
entry_conditions: Claude Code supports HTTP hook type
exit_conditions: Metrics posted to localhost endpoint on every tool call
Payload includes: tool_name, duration_ms, success, tokens_used
Dashboard endpoint receives and stores metrics
units.rollback: Remove HTTP hook entries from settings.json

steps.instruction: Define HTTP hook in settings.json: type='http', url='http://localhost:18370/metrics', method='POST'
Configure payload template: {tool, duration, success, tokens, timestamp, session_id}
Set timeout: 2s, fail-open (don't block on endpoint failure)
Create minimal Express endpoint at port 18370 to receive and store metrics
Test with tool calls and verify metrics received

deliverables.description: Minimal Express server receiving hook telemetry on port 18370

units.title: Migrate top 5 bash checks to prompt hooks
units.rationale: Several bash hooks perform text analysis that LLMs handle better — semantic intent detection, quality assessment, pattern recognition. Migrating these improves accuracy and maintainability.
entry_conditions: Prompt hook type proven working from P0-U01 through P0-U03
exit_conditions: 5 bash checks migrated to prompt hooks
Accuracy improved or maintained for each
Bash fallbacks preserved for offline mode

steps.instruction: Audit pretooluse-unified.sh and posttooluse-unified.sh for text-analysis checks
Identify top 5 candidates: Agent simple-query warn, grep-on-just-read warn, compound command deny, test-file read warn, catalog-file read warn
Write prompt templates for each, handling edge cases better than regex
Test migrated hooks against historical false positive/negative cases
Keep bash versions as fallback, add prompt hooks as primary

units.title: Hook type selection guide
units.rationale: With 4 hook types (command, prompt, agent, HTTP) developers need a decision framework to choose the right type for each use case.
entry_conditions: All 4 hook types implemented and tested
exit_conditions: Guide documented in debugging-patterns.md
Decision tree covers: latency needs, complexity, offline support, cost
Examples for each hook type included

Include latency/cost comparison table
Add migration checklist for converting between types
Include examples from each implemented hook
